title: The Midnight Click
text: I installed a premium home security camera to watch my front porch. Last night at 3:14 AM, my phone pinged with a motion alert. The video showed a tall man in a trench coat walking up to my door. He didn't knock or try the handle. Instead, he stared directly into the lens, pulled a phone out of his pocket, and tapped the screen. In that exact millisecond, my phone in my hand buzzed with a notification stating that my guest had arrived. I looked through the peephole, but the porch was empty. When I checked the live feed again, the man was standing inside my hallway, staring up at the indoor camera, tapping his phone a second time asdasdasdasd asdasdsad asdsadsad asdasdsad asdsadsad try again askdaskdaskd laskdlkasdlk asdklsakdlk.

title: The Filter
text: My sister was testing a new facial filter app on her phone late last night. The app was designed to add cute animal ears and noses to anyone in the frame. She held the phone up to take a selfie in her dark bedroom. The screen immediately locked onto her face, adding the filter. A second later, the app detected five more invisible faces crowding tightly around her shoulder, covering them all in cartoon masks.

title: The Passenger Seat
text: My car's smart navigation system began malfunctioning during a midnight drive through the countryside. The digital map displayed a small, blue arrow representing my vehicle moving down the empty highway. Suddenly, a second blue arrow appeared on the screen, positioned exactly one inch behind mine. I checked my rearview mirror, but the road behind me was pitch black and completely vacant. The GPS voice suddenly spoke over the speakers, its tone completely flat: 'In 500 meters, your passenger will take the wheel.' I heard the unmistakable click of the passenger side seatbelt buckling itself into place.
